channel.title: BookByte
channel.description: Plain-English bookkeeping and tax guides for the self-employed: freelancers, contractors, creators and single-owner LLCs and S-corps.

item.title: Can AI do your accounting? What it gets right and wrong
item.description: Can AI do your accounting? See which bookkeeping tasks AI handles well, where it gets things wrong, and a simple test to check it on your own books.

item.title: IRS FIRE is closing: e-file 1099s with IRIS instead
item.description: IRS FIRE stops taking 1099s on Nov. 19, 2026. How to get an IRIS TCC now, e-file 1099-NECs free in IRIS, and use AI to prep your vendor list safely.

item.title: AI bank reconciliation: how to do it and what AI can’t do
item.description: Use AI for bank reconciliation: copy-paste prompts to match your books to your statement, find missing and duplicate lines, and check the result yourself.

item.title: QuickBooks AI banking suggestions: review before you post
item.description: What the green, blue and orange QuickBooks AI banking signals mean, when to use Ready to post, and a month-end check that catches wrong matches.

item.title: AI prompts to categorize business transactions (copy-paste)
item.description: Copy-and-paste AI prompts to categorize business transactions into Schedule C lines, flag personal charges and catch mistakes before they hit your books.

item.title: Quarterly estimated taxes in California: a 2026 guide
item.description: Who must pay California estimated tax, IRS and FTB due dates for 2026, the 30/40/0/30 schedule and safe harbor rules, with a worked example.

item.title: How to use AI for bookkeeping, and keep your books accurate
item.description: Use AI for bookkeeping without wrong numbers: a 3-pass method to categorize transactions, read receipts and close the month, with a prompt to copy.
